chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Qasim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Musa ibn Zanjawiya al-Tafleysi, from Abu Umar al-Hannat, from Ismail al-Sayqal al-Razi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and with me were two garments. He said to me: 'O Abu Ismail! Many garments come to me from your side, but these two garments that you are carrying do not come to me like them.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, the mother of Ismail spun them, and I wove them.' He said to me: 'A weaver?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not be a weaver.' I said: 'Then what should I be?' He said: 'Be a polisher.' And there were two hundred dirhams with me, so I bought swords and old mirrors with them, and I arrived in Rayy with them, and I sold them for a great profit.
ai.seo_question: What profession did Imam al-Sadiq recommend to Ismail al-Sayqal and why?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s practical wisdom in guiding Ismail al-Sayqal to leverage his specific skill of weaving to produce high-quality goods for trade, rather than merely performing the labor of weaving itself. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on professional specialization and commercial acumen, illustrating how mastering a craft can lead to financial success and social mobility within the early Islamic community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Qasim Bin Is’haq Bin Ibrahim, from Musa Bin Zanjawiya Al Tafleysi, from Abu Umar Al Hannat, from Ismail Al Sayqal Al Razy who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and with me were two clothes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Ismail! The ones before you have come to me<sup>asws</sup> with numerous clothes and they did not come to me<sup>asws</sup> with the likes of these two clothes which you are carrying’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The mother of Ismail spun these two, and I weaved these two’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘(You are) a weaver?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not become a weaver’. I said, ‘So what should I become?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Become a polisher’. And there were two hundred Dirhams with me, so I bought swords with it, and old mirrors, and proceded with these to Al-Rayy, and I sold these (after polishing them) for a lot of profit’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘ Abd Allah from al-Qasim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from Musa ibn Zanjawayh al-Taflisiy from abu ‘Amr al-Hannat from ‘Isma’il al-Sayqal al-Raziy who has said the following:

“Once I visited abu ’Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam. I had two pieces of fabric materials with me. He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu Tsma’il, from your area people bring us many kinds of fabrics but not like these two pieces that you carry.’ I said, T pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, the mother of Tsma’il prepares threads and I weave them.’ He (the Imam) asked, ’Are you a weaver?’ I replied, ’Yes, I am a weaver.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not be a weaver.’ I then asked, ‘What kind of work then I should do?’ He (the Imam) said, ’Work as a sword polisher.’ I had two hundred dirhams with me with which I purchased swords and sold. I took them to al-Rayy, sold them and made a large profit.’”
